title: Minimum Number of Operations to Reinitialize a Permutation
summary: Given an even integer n, you start with a permutation perm where perm[i] equals i.
statement: Given an even integer n, you start with a permutation perm where perm[i] equals i. An operation involves creating a new array arr by setting arr[i] based on perm[i] values. The operation is repeated until the permutation returns to its initial state. The task is to find the minimum number of such operations needed.
constraints: n is even and the initial permutation is [0,1,...,n-1].
Apply the stated even/odd index rearrangement until the full permutation first returns; return the positive operation count.
hints: Positions zero and n-1 never move; track the orbit of position one.
Derive its next position from whether it lies in the first or second half.
Count transitions until position one returns to itself.
The shuffle is a permutation, and its nontrivial positions share the cycle order governing restoration; the orbit length of one is the first full reset.
editorial: The shuffle is a permutation, and its nontrivial positions share the cycle order governing restoration; the orbit length of one is the first full reset.
